text: Today's practice (first on Home and on the Practice page): one mixed round of 12 questions made from what you got wrong in the drills (Fill the blank, Transform, Word pairs, Sound words, Vocabulary, Pictures, Signs and the two new drills), newest first. A right answer takes the item off that drill's mistakes. When you have few mistakes, new questions at your level fill the round. Your best score for the day is saved.

Find the mistake (Practice, Grammar drills): 200 sentences from N5 to N2, each with one wrong word (a particle, a verb or adjective form, a tense, a counter, a giving or receiving verb, keigo). Tap the wrong word, then see the sentence put right with its sound, its meaning and the reason. The wrong sentence is never read aloud.

Listen and reply (Practice, Listening): hear a line and choose the natural reply. 160 exchanges: 80 everyday and workplace (greetings and set replies, offers, invitations, thanks and apologies, phone, shop) and 80 clinical, where you answer a patient, a relative, a nurse or a senior doctor. The clinical answers model good practice: acknowledge first, ask openly, promise nothing, and ask directly and gently when someone hints at wanting to die or disappear.

Listening practice now has every practice case: the whole interview and five questions for the eight older admission cases, the eight older discharge cases and the four end-of-treatment reviews (100 new questions). Each case page links to its listening.
After opening the Body map or a picture print sheet, a tap on a later page could redraw that page. Fixed.
The Practice page has a Listening section. All new Japanese is a draft until a native Japanese-speaking clinician reviews it.
